main_text.p: brofedigaeth namyn gwared ni rhag diwg. Amen. Hoc est:

p.i: Noster pater, qui es in ipsis cœlis: sanctifice-tur nomen tuum: adveniat illud regnum tuum: fiat tua voluntas super illam terram sicut & in illo cœlo: nostrum panem quotidianum da nobis hodie, & remitte nobis nostra debita, sicut etiam remittimus debitoribus nostris. Et ne indu-cas nos in tentationem, sed libera nos a malo, Amen.

main_text.p: ¶CAMBRICA lingua eadem, quae vetus Britannica[?]; quam vide.

¶CAPPADOCVM lingua Barbaram esseCappadocum lingua bar-bara. conjicio vel ex mensium nominibus duodecim, quae sunt, Τίριξ, Μάτα, Ξανανθικοί, Μίθρι, Απομεναμα[?], Αρθεχά[?], Τιθυσία, Ωρμένια[?], Σόνδεχ[?], Αρτάνια[?], Αρπεσίν[?], Αρμιόταλα[?].
Cappadocces mirantur Apostolos suâ lingua loquentes Hierosolymis in Pentecoste.

¶CARES Homerus in Catalogo priva-tim βαρβαροφώνες appellavit: non quiaDe lingua Carica, de que barba-ris & barbarismo in univer-sum, & stra bonis li 14. Cariæ lingua brevissima sit (quod non est: nam permulta Græca nomina admixta habet, ut Philippus testatur Caricarum re-rum conscriptor:) sed ego arbitror ab initio confiso nomine, eos barbaros appellatos,Barbari. qui difficulter, asperè ac duriter loqueren-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek names in the Cappadocian list are only partly legible and are marked [?]. "Britannica" is partly damaged. The note "De lingua Carica..." is hard to read at its line breaks; "que barba-ris" and "stra bonis li 14" are doubtful. The word "confiso" is copied as printed and may be a printing error for "confuso". "Cappadocces" is printed as it stands, probably a printing error for "Cappadoces". The paragraph about Cares breaks off at the foot of the page at "loqueren-". Greek and Hebrew are in their own letters.
